record.original_question: For the variable-gap deletion problem in which one seeks a recursive description for a Cantor set generated from a sequence (α_n)_{n≥1}, determine how the answer changes when bilateral symmetry of the construction is enforced and how it changes when that symmetry is relaxed.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $(\alpha_n)_{n\geq 1}$ be a sequence of real numbers with $0<\alpha_n<1$ for every $n$ and
$$1-\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}2^{n-1}\alpha_n\;\geq\;0.$$
Define a Cantor-type subset $C=C((\alpha_n))$ of $[0,1]$ by the following inductive deletion procedure. Set $C_0=[0,1]$. If $C_{n-1}$ is the disjoint union of $2^{n-1}$ closed intervals of equal length, obtain $C_n$ by removing from each of these $2^{n-1}$ intervals an open subinterval of length $\alpha_n\cdot\ell_{n-1}$, where $\ell_{n-1}$ is the length of each component of $C_{n-1}$ (so the deleted gap at stage $n$ has total measure $2^{n-1}\alpha_n$ when $\ell_0=1$, or more generally one removes a gap of length $\alpha_n$ from each component when normalized appropriately). Set $C=\bigcap_{n\geq 0}C_n$.

(a) (Symmetric case.) Assuming that at every stage $n$ the deleted open interval is centered at the midpoint of its parent component (bilateral symmetry), give an explicit recursive descriptive formula characterizing the points of $C$ — for example, in the form of a base-dependent digit expansion or an arithmetic membership criterion expressed directly in terms of the sequence $(\alpha_n)$.

(b) (Asymmetric case.) Determine how the descriptive formula of (a) must be modified when the requirement of bilateral symmetry is dropped, i.e., when at stage $n$ the deleted open interval inside each parent component is allowed to be placed off-center (subject only to remaining a proper open subinterval of length $\alpha_n$ times the parent length). Specify what additional parameters are needed, and identify which features of the symmetric description persist and which must change.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an explicit open problem in a recent (2025) survey on set-theoretic descriptions of Cantor sets, where variable-gap deletions and the role of symmetry versus asymmetry are listed among the unresolved directions. No published resolution providing a recursive description in either the symmetric or asymmetric variable-gap setting was found.
